PR #25877 title: BUG: Include broadcasting for rtol argument in matrix_rank

category_specific_evidence: The bug concerns broadcasting of the rtol argument in numpy.linalg.matrix_rank (PR#25877, gh-25877), where rtol as a list or array was not broadcast against stacked matrices.
Regression test x = np.zeros((4, 3, 2)) with rtol given as 0.0, [0.0]*4, or np.zeros((4,)) asserts result shape (4,).
Original code computed rtol only when None and applied tol = S.max(axis=-1, keepdims=True) * rtol without broadcasting rtol per matrix; the fix adds asarray(rtol)[..., newaxis] for the rtol path.
A reviewer noted the test would not have failed without the fix and suggested an explicit example from the issue; a further test asserts matrix_rank(I, tol=0.0) equals matrix_rank(I, rtol=0.0).
Final version of the fix uses rtol = broadcast_to(rtol, A.shape[:-2])[..., newaxis] after the None default, and the tol/rtol mutual-exclusion ValueError is moved before the svd call.
Default rtol when unspecified is max(A.shape[-2:]) * finfo(S.dtype).eps, per the diff.
reproduction_risks: The exact numerical values expected in the issue were not included in the passages; the test only checks output shape, not rank values.
The discussion shows an intermediate version using asarray(rtol)[..., newaxis] that was superseded by broadcast_to, so the two versions may behave differently for some inputs.
Passing both tol and rtol must raise ValueError; reproduction should not set both.
Specific dtype, precision and tolerance values for the assertions are not stated in the passages.
